planting.note: Plant a rooted crown, sucker, or slip after all frost danger has passed into fast-draining, humus-rich soil in full sun; Victoria has been grown on Réunion Island since its introduction in the late 1600s and is traditionally set at high density on free-draining volcanic slopes.

directions: Victoria is the small, intensely sweet pineapple that dominates Réunion Island's orchards and remains the island's most valuable exported fruit, grown traditionally at close spacing on well-drained volcanic hillsides. The fruit rarely exceeds about two pounds, ripening to a deep golden-yellow rind with juicy, melting, low-fiber flesh and a core tender enough to eat along with the rest of the fruit. Give plants gritty, fast-draining soil and full sun, and let the soil dry between waterings since the rosette of stiff leaves stores water efficiently. A single planting can be kept in production across several successive fruiting cycles by leaving basal suckers to replace the mother plant after each harvest.
sources: CIRAD (Centre de coopération internationale en recherche agronomique pour le développement) — Agritrop Repository, Réunion pineapple studies
CIRAD COSAQ — Technical Fact Sheets on Victoria Pineapple Production in Réunion

common_name: Makalioka Rice (Madagascar Alaotra Luxury Long-Grain Rice)

planting.note: Direct sow into flooded or consistently saturated paddy soil once the soil has warmed well past the last frost; Makalioka 34 is strongly photoperiod-sensitive and times its flowering to the local Alaotra growing season, so outside Madagascar it needs a long, uninterrupted warm season to reach maturity.

directions: Makalioka 34 is a farmer- and FOFIFA-selected long-grain rice from the Lac Alaotra basin, Madagascar's principal rice-growing region, released from local selection lines in the early twentieth century and still regarded by many Malagasy consumers as the country's finest-eating rice. The grain is long, slender, and translucent, cooking up with a fragrant, slightly sweet flavor that commands a price premium in Madagascar's domestic market. Keep the paddy or garden bed continuously flooded or saturated through the long vegetative cycle, since the variety is slow to mature and sensitive to day length, flowering only as daylight hours shorten toward the local autumn. Harvest once the heavy seed heads droop and turn golden, then dry thoroughly before milling to preserve the prized long, clear grain.
sources: FOFIFA (Centre National de Recherche Appliquée au Développement Rural), Madagascar
Cornell International Institute for Food, Agriculture and Development — rice varietal diffusion studies in Madagascar

planting.note: Set out rhizome divisions or container-grown plants once all frost danger has passed into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in filtered light; longoza grows naturally at middle elevations in Madagascar's humid eastern forests and does not tolerate drought or cold.

directions: Longoza is a tall, reed-like ginger relative native to Madagascar's humid forest margins, long valued by rural Malagasy communities as a source of quick energy on long hunting or walking treks because of the sugary, sour-sweet pulp packed around its seeds. The crushed dried seeds are used as a peppery, aromatic spice in their own right and are sometimes added to coffee during roasting for extra fragrance. Clumps spread by thick rhizomes into substantial stands of upright, leafy pseudostems, so give the planting ample room and protect it from harsh midday sun, which can scorch the broad leaves. Keep soil consistently moist and humid year-round, and harvest ripe berries as they split open to reveal the seed-covered pulp inside.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew — Plants of the World Online
FOFIFA (Centre National de Recherche Appliquée au Développement Rural), Madagascar

common_name: Piment Cabri (Réunion Island Strawberry-Shaped Habanero-Type Chili)

planting.note: Start seed on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay warm; Piment Cabri is traditionally grown in the cool, misty highlands of Salazie on Réunion Island.

directions: Piment Cabri takes its name from its oval, wrinkled, strawberry-like pods, a traditional Réunion Island Habanero-type chili long grown in the cool, cloud-wrapped highlands around Salazie. Its intense, fruity aroma and sharp heat make it a favorite for seasoning rougail and carri, the island's signature Creole dishes, used sparingly to perfume a dish rather than overwhelm it. Pods ripen from green through yellow to a deep orange-red, and plants perform best with warm days but appreciate relief from the most intense midday sun during long hot summers away from Réunion's cooler highland microclimate. Pick regularly through the season to keep plants flowering and producing, and handle ripe pods with care given their habanero-level heat.
sources: Conservatoire Botanique National de Mascarin, Réunion

planting.note: Plant a young tree in spring in full sun in deep, well-drained soil; José is strongly polyembryonic and comes true from seed, so Réunion growers commonly plant seedling trees rather than grafted stock.

directions: José is the dominant mango of Réunion Island, filling more than half the island's mango orchards and prized by Réunionnais households for its rounded, roughly half-pound fruit that ripens from green to yellow with pink-red blush. The firm, fiberless, deep orange flesh carries a rich, highly fragrant sweetness that local cooks and fruit sellers rate above most imported commercial cultivars. Because the variety is strongly polyembryonic, seedling trees grow true to type, which is why many Réunion growers raise José from seed rather than grafting, though grafted stock establishes and bears sooner. Give trees deep, well-drained soil and full sun, and watch closely for local fruit fly and anthracnose pressure, to which José is notably susceptible, timing harvest and orchard sanitation accordingly.
sources: CIRAD (Centre de coopération internationale en recherche agronomique pour le développement) — Agritrop Repository, Réunion mango variety trials
CIRAD COSAQ — Technical Fact Sheets on Mango Production in Réunion
